title: Actual reconstruction maps for normalized strict systems
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-pc-scheme]. On a fixed small skeleton of its pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], put $B_{n,W}=(R/\varpi^n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\varprojlim_n B_{n,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear $B_{n,W}$-module systems, with componentwise morphisms, of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and use its unbounded derived category. Write $\mathscr N_W$ for the full subcategory with all transition adjoints $N_m\otimes^L_{B_{m,W}}B_{n,W}\to N_n$ invertible for $m\ge n$, and $\mathscr C_W\subset D(\widehat R_W)$ for the full subcategory of derived-complete complexes [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-derived-complete]. No cohomological bound, constructibility, uniform Tor interval or equipped local model is assumed.

Use the specified adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W=R\lim\circ U_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], with its actual unit $u$ and counit $e$. Then $\mathcal R_W(P)$ is normalized for every ambient $P\in D(\widehat R_W)$. For every normalized $N\in D(\mathscr S_W)$, $\mathcal L_WN$ is derived complete and the actual map $e_N:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WN\to N$ is an isomorphism of derived strict systems. At every level $n$, its evaluation is the scalar-extension adjoint $(\mathcal L_WN)\otimes^L_{\widehat R_W}B_{n,W}\to N_n$ of the specified total-limit projection. For every derived-complete $K$, the actual unit $u_K:K\to\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_WK$ is an isomorphism. These maps are natural in $N$ and $K$, with the triangle identities of the specified adjunction; there are no boundedness, constructibility or Tor-amplitude hypotheses.

proof.text:
Choose the single flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to P$ supplied by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Its strict quotient system represents $\mathcal R_WP$. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], $Q\otimes_{\widehat R_W}B_m$ is K-flat over $B_m$; hence [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes its next derived reduction by ordinary tensor. The adjoint of the actual quotient transition is the balancing isomorphism
$$(Q\otimes_{\widehat R_W}B_m)\otimes_{B_m}B_n\longrightarrow Q\otimes_{\widehat R_W}B_n,\quad (x\otimes b)\otimes a\longmapsto x\otimes q_{m,n}(b)a.$$
Its inverse is $x\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes a$. Both composites are identities by balancing, and these formulas commute with differentials and restrictions. For three indices both composites multiply the two quotient scalars in the same order. Thus these are the adjoints of the specified transitions, with their cocycle, so $\mathcal R_WP$ is normalized as defined in [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower].

proof.text: For normalized $N\in D(\mathscr S_W)$, its restriction $U_WN$ is the coherent underlying $\widehat R_W$-tower required by [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]: the coherence is supplied by the strict system itself. Its levels and transition adjoints are exactly the ones in that definition. By [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], its total limit is $M=\mathcal L_WN$. Apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] to this tower. It says that $M$ is derived complete and that, for each $n\geq1$, the scalar-extension adjunct $c_n:M\otimes^L_{\widehat R_W}B_n\to N_n$ of the specified total-limit projection is an isomorphism. This is its canonical counit comparison, rather than an arbitrarily chosen finite-level isomorphism. The lemma imposes no boundedness or constructibility condition.

source.place: §3.5, Lemma 3.5.7(1)–(5), especially the unbounded regular-ideal case (5); actual maps are those of the sequence-topos adjunction in (1).

proof.text: The actual counit $e_N$ is already a morphism in $D(\mathscr S_W)$, by [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The same statement identifies its $n$th evaluation with the scalar-extension adjunct of the total-limit projection, hence with $c_n$ from Step 2, for the specified adjunction. Every such evaluation is invertible. The joint detection of isomorphisms by derived evaluations, asserted in that node, therefore makes $e_N$ itself invertible. This establishes invertibility in the derived strict-system category without attempting to lift an arbitrary compatible family of level maps.

source.place: §3.5, Lemma 3.5.7(1)–(5), especially the unbounded regular-ideal case (5); actual maps are those of the sequence-topos adjunction in (1).

proof.text: The coefficient hypotheses needed to apply [lem-pur-roos-intrinsic-completeness-equivalence] hold for $A=R$, $t=\varpi$, $T=W$. Indeed [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] says that $R$ is a principal ideal domain and $\varpi\ne0$, so every ideal is finitely generated and multiplication by $\varpi^n$ is injective. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], all $R/(\varpi^n)$ are finite; in particular $R/(\varpi)$ is torsion as an additive group. The exact sequence $0\to R\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R\to R/(\varpi^n)\to0$ represents each quotient by a bounded complex of finite free modules, hence makes it perfect by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. These verify precisely the Noetherian, finite-quotient, perfect-quotient and torsion assumptions of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. The auxiliary prime $p\ne\ell$ in the completeness-equivalence lemma can be chosen arbitrarily; its statement imposes no characteristic condition on $W$. Its completed sheaf and strict reductions are expressly the constant-quotient presentation used here.

source.place: §3.5, Lemma 3.5.7(1)–(5), especially the unbounded regular-ideal case (5); actual maps are those of the sequence-topos adjunction in (1).

proof.text: Let $K$ be derived complete and put $N=\mathcal R_WK$; it is normalized by Step 1, so Steps 2--3 make $e_N$ invertible. The triangle identity $\mathcal L_W(e_N)\circ u_{\mathcal L_WN}=1$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] then shows that $u_{\mathcal L_WN}=\mathcal L_W(e_N)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Next, by the same node $N$ is the strict system $(Q\otimes_{\widehat R_W}B_n)_n$ on one flat-term K-flat representative $Q\to K$, and $\mathcal L_WN=R\lim U_WN$ is the total derived limit of exactly the strict reductions $\operatorname{Res}_nK_n$ formed on that same $Q$ in [lem-pur-roos-intrinsic-completeness-equivalence]. With the coefficient hypotheses verified in Step 4, the implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(v) of that lemma makes the canonical augmentation $\varphi=\operatorname{comp}_K:K\to\mathcal L_WN$ an isomorphism. Only its invertibility is used; $\varphi$ is not identified with $u_K$. Naturality of $u$ applied to $\varphi$ gives $\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_W(\varphi)\circ u_K=u_{\mathcal L_WN}\circ\varphi$. The right side and $\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_W(\varphi)$ are isomorphisms, hence $u_K=\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_W(\varphi)^{-1}\circ u_{\mathcal L_WN}\circ\varphi$ is an isomorphism. Thus the actual unit is invertible without comparing two maps into a homotopy limit through their projections, and without identifying the specified adjunction with another one.

source.place: §3.5, Lemma 3.5.7(1)–(5), especially the unbounded regular-ideal case (5); actual maps are those of the sequence-topos adjunction in (1).

proof.text: The transformations used throughout are the unit $u$ and counit $e$ of the one adjunction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], which already asserts their naturality and triangle identities in the derived system categories. Thus for $a:N\to N'$ and $b:K\to K'$ their squares read $a\circ e_N=e_{N'}\circ\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_W(a)$ and $\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_W(b)\circ u_K=u_{K'}\circ b$. Its identities remain $e_{\mathcal R_WP}\circ\mathcal R_W(u_P)=1$ and $\mathcal L_W(e_N)\circ u_{\mathcal L_WN}=1$. Steps 1–5 show that the relevant objects lie in the stated full subcategories and that these same components are invertible there. Restricting these equalities proves all requested naturality and triangle assertions, with no additional hypotheses.
